messages:
pagerbot: PAGER: auth-proxy rate anomaly detected -> 401/403 spike from ~120 unique IPs, correlated with increased log writes to /var/log/proxy/*. Severity: P1. Paging oncall-kai.

oncall-kai: I'm on it. grabbing initial signals. which regions? :eyes:

pagerbot: spike started 03:12 UTC. sources: us-west-2 + eu-central. avg 401s up x40 vs baseline. some requests include suspicious long querystrings.

oncall-kai: confirming with infra. oliver? can you pull last 15m of proxy access logs and grep for repeated bearer patterns?

infra-oliver: pulling now. quick sample shows repeated header pattern: "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci..." across many tokens, many short-lived. also seeing logs sent to s3-archive-staging around same time.

sec-eng-maya: thanks. hypothesis: token replay/credential stuffing or leaked debug logs. we should assume tokens may be compromised until proven otherwise. recommend immediate short-term mitigations: 1) block known abusive IPs at edge 2) enable 429 rate-limit on proxy 3) disable log-forwarder to external bucket 4) start targeted key rotation for affected service tokens.

eng-sre-noah: on (1)+(2) now: added WAF IP blocklist for top 50 offending IPs, enabled 429 threshold at 2r/s per src IP. pushing change to edge (canary -> global in 2m).

prod-ops-lina: stopped the log-forwarder to s3-archive-staging and set retention to quarantine. good call. capturing a copy to internal secure bucket for forensics.

cs-amy: any customer impact yet? are we seeing failed user requests or timeouts reported?

oncall-kai: some customer requests are getting 401s where they previously succeeded (~0.5% of traffic for a handful of tenants). likely caused by token invalidation or rate limits. we should prepare a customer communication template.

legal-jay: flagging legal. if PII or auth tokens were included in the copied logs to external bucket, we need to start notification timeline and preserve chain-of-custody. please do not delete forensic copies.

sec-eng-maya: data-scope: initial sample shows headers + URL querystrings in forwarded logs. potential token snippets present. mark as data-exposure candidate. we need to rotate any long-lived service tokens immediately and revoke suspicious sessions.

infra-oliver: query to find affected service principals: 
```
# find tokens used in last 2h
zcat /var/log/proxy/access.log.*.gz | grep -E "Authorization: Bearer" | awk -F"Bearer " '{print $2}' | cut -d' ' -f1 | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head
```
produced ~120 token hashes; cross-referencing with token service now.

eng-sre-noah: I'm coordinating with auth-service to revoke the top 20 tokens immediately. rolling rotation for service accounts in affected pool. will post back with token IDs.

prod-ops-lina: running canary on token revocation to avoid mass-customer disruption. targeting internal service accounts first, then non-critical tenants.

cs-amy: prepping support threads and customer FAQ. recommended messaging: brief outage risk, we rotated some service tokens, users may need to re-auth for a short window, no confirmed customer data exfil yet, investigation ongoing.

legal-jay: good. preserve timeline in incident doc and start initial notification draft for security/privacy team review.

sec-eng-maya: action items summary: 
- edge: IP block + rate limit (no rollback unless clear)
- infra: stop external log-forwarder, preserve quarantine copy
- auth: revoke top suspicious tokens + rotate service keys, enable short-lived tokens where possible
- eng-sre: monitor error rates and latency, rollback thresholds set (if >5% user impact cancel further revokes)
- cs/legal: prepare comms and notification if confirmed exposure

oncall-kai: timeline: T+0m detect -> T+4m edge mitigations live -> T+10m log-forwarder off -> T+20m token revokes started. next update in 15m or earlier if customer impact >1%.

eng-sre-noah: added alert: auth.failed.rate > 5% for >5m -> @pagerbot escalate to SRE and SecEng.

prod-ops-lina: snapshotting affected servers and taking forensic notes. tagging instance IDs in incident doc.

cs-amy: creating customer ticket template and drafting notice for impacted customers in case rollback triggers mass re-auth.

sec-eng-maya: once revokes finish we should run a re-ingest check for any tokens in external bucket. if present, escalate to legal for notification cadence.

oncall-kai: thanks team. staying on channel. will run handoff to overnight oncall at T+8h if still open. :thumbsup:

pagerbot: INCIDENT LOGGED: incident_id=INC-2026-047, channel=incidents, priority=P1. all actions captured to incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-047 (do not click if you are not on the incident roster).

legal-jay: added required evidence preservation checklist.

sec-eng-maya: small note — postmortem owners: sec-eng + eng-sre. let's keep remediation tickets actionable: enforce no-forwarding of headers in log-forwarders, scrub tokens at ingestion, and short-lived service tokens by default.

oncall-kai: update: auth team reported 18 revoked tokens mapped to internal services, 3 mapped to external customers (we're triaging customer mapping now).

cs-amy: prepping targeted outreach for those 3 customers; legal looped for privacy review.

eng-sre-noah: monitoring looks stable after revokes, 401 spike down to x3 baseline. keeping rate-limits and blocks in place for now.

prod-ops-lina: leaving quarantine copy isolated, no further external access.

sec-eng-maya: thanks. if anything changes call out immediately. otherwise we'll transition to after-action planning in 2 hours.

oncall-kai: handing off to night oncall @oncall-zoe at 23:00 UTC with summary in the incident doc. good work.

pagerbot: PAGE: incident update posted to incident doc.
